title: Which AI Engine Should You Optimize For First?
metaTitle: Which AI Engine Should You Optimize For First?
metaDescription: Optimize for ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews first — where your buyers already are. Learn how the major AI engines differ and how to prioritize with data.
primaryKeyword: which ai engine should i optimize for first
shortAnswer: Optimize first for the engine your buyers actually use — for most B2B and consumer audiences, that's ChatGPT (the broadest reach of any AI assistant) and Google's AI Overviews (sitting on top of the search engine everyone already opens). Perplexity matters more if your buyers research before they buy. The good news: the foundational work — answer-shaped content, a clear entity, third-party consensus — carries across all of them, so you rarely have to commit to just one for long.
intro: Every AEO plan eventually runs into the same fork in the road: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude — where do you actually start? Most teams pick one of two bad options. They freeze, waiting for someone to hand them a definitive ranking of engines. Or they scatter a thin layer of effort across all five and wonder six months later why none of them moved. Neither works, and neither is necessary. The honest answer is that the 'best' engine to optimize for is whichever one already sits between your buyers and their decision — and that's something you can find out with data, not a hunch.

sections.heading: Which AI Engine Should You Optimize For First?
sections.body:
The one your buyers already use to research and buy — for most companies that means ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews before Perplexity or Claude. Match the engine to how your specific audience actually behaves, not to whichever one is loudest in the news that week.

A quick way to decide:
- If you sell to consumers or generalist B2B buyers, start with ChatGPT. It's the assistant people open out of habit, and it's increasingly willing to name specific brands and products when someone asks a buying question directly.
- If your buyers still start their research on Google, start with AI Overviews. You're not chasing a new channel — you're defending the one you already show up in.
- If your buyers are researchers, developers, or analysts who check sources before they trust an answer, weight Perplexity higher than its size suggests. It's built around citations, and that audience notices them.

You don't need certainty to start, just a reasonable read on your own buyers. The next section explains why that first guess matters less than most people assume.

sections.heading: How the Major AI Engines Differ
sections.body:
ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, and Perplexity pull from different sources and reward different signals, so 'optimizing for AI' is never really one single task. Knowing the differences helps you set expectations for what shows up where.

- ChatGPT: leans on browsing and search-augmented answers, has one of the largest active user bases of any conversational assistant, and will increasingly recommend specific brands in response to buying questions rather than staying generic.
- Google AI Overviews / Gemini: grounded in Google's own search index and knowledge graph, so pages that already rank well in classic Google search have a real head start here.
- Perplexity: built around citations. It shows exactly which pages an answer came from, and it rewards content that reads like a well-sourced answer over content that reads like a landing page.

For a fuller breakdown of what each engine rewards and how to check where you stand in each one, see our guide to [the best AI search engines to optimize for](/blog/best-ai-search-engines). The differences matter less for what you write, though, and more for where you go to check results — which brings us to the part that's genuinely shared.

sections.heading: The Shared Foundation Carries Across Engines
sections.body:
The core AEO work — direct answers, a clearly defined entity, consistent facts repeated across the web — lifts your visibility in ChatGPT, AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude at roughly the same time. Picking 'first' is a question of sequencing effort, not permanently ignoring the rest.

That's because these engines draw on overlapping raw material: your own site, third-party reviews, comparison pages, forum threads, structured data. Fix the following once and every engine benefits:
- Answer-first structure — open every important page and section with a direct one- to two-sentence answer instead of throat-clearing.
- Entity clarity — one consistent brand name, one clear definition of what you do, backed by structured data.
- Third-party consensus — reviews, comparisons, and independent mentions that repeat the same facts about you in their own words.

This is the same groundwork covered in our guide to [AI search optimization](/blog/ai-search-optimization) — worth reading before you spend a dollar on engine-specific tactics, because most of what moves the needle isn't engine-specific at all.

sections.heading: How to Decide With Data, Not Guesswork
sections.body:
Don't guess — audit which engines already mention your brand, compare that against which engines your buyers actually open, and start with the engine where the gap is biggest and the buyer overlap is highest. That single comparison beats any generic ranking of engines by popularity.

A simple process:
1. Run an audit across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini / Google AI Overviews to see where you currently show up — and where you're invisible.
2. Cross-reference against your own funnel signals: referral traffic from perplexity.ai, mentions of 'I asked ChatGPT' in sales calls, support tickets that reference an AI answer.
3. Prioritize the engine with the largest gap between 'buyers who use it' and 'AI mentions you actually get there.' That gap is your highest-leverage first move.

Look at an [example AEOeye report](/example) to see what this comparison looks like in practice — where a brand shows up across engines and where it quietly doesn't. Then [run a free audit](/#audit) to see exactly which AI engines already mention you, and which ones need work first.

keyTakeaways: Optimize first for the engine your buyers actually use — usually ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews, not whichever engine is trending.
ChatGPT rewards broad reach and browsing-augmented answers; Google AI Overviews rewards your existing search rankings; Perplexity rewards citations.
The foundational AEO work — answer-first content, entity clarity, third-party consensus — lifts every engine at roughly the same time.
Don't pick blind: audit where you already show up, then compare it against where your buyers actually search.
'First' means sequencing your effort, not permanently ignoring the other engines.
Revisit your priority every few months — which engine your buyers open first shifts faster than most SEO channels do.

faqs.q: Should I optimize for ChatGPT or Google first?
faqs.a: Start with whichever one your buyers already open. For most companies with mixed B2B and consumer audiences, that's ChatGPT for direct assistant use and Google AI Overviews for search-driven queries. If you can only sequence one, start with the engine that shows the bigger visibility gap in an audit.

faqs.q: Do I need to optimize for every AI engine?
faqs.a: Not separately. The core work — answer-shaped content, entity clarity, third-party consensus — benefits ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Overviews, and Claude at the same time, so you're rarely choosing one engine at the total exclusion of the others.

faqs.q: Which AI engine has the most users?
faqs.a: ChatGPT is widely reported to have one of the largest active user bases among conversational AI assistants, though Google's AI Overviews likely reaches a larger audience by volume simply because it's embedded directly inside Google Search results.

faqs.q: Does optimizing for one engine help the others?
faqs.a: Yes, mostly. These engines draw on overlapping web content, third-party reviews, and structured data, so work that makes you clearer and more citable for one engine tends to lift your visibility in the others too.
